In recent years, this dual formulation has turned out to be powerful and useful for various problems related to the equilibrium and decentralization in economics. See Ekeland (2005, 2010), Carlier (2010), Chiappori et al. (2010), Chernozhukov et al. (2010), and Galichon and Salani´ e (2012). In econometrics, Galichon and Henry (2009) and Ekeland et al. (2010) showed that the dual formulation yields a test statistic for a set of theoretical restrictions in partially identified economic models.
